note: WHERE THIS EDITION'S PAGE IMAGES ARE: ONE archive item, TWO printed volumes of the work. Re-sourced 2026-10-05 onto the copy whose OCR this edition's transcription now IS. Taylor's 1816 edition divides the work over two volumes: vol. I carries it entire from its title page to Book V ch. XXXIX (printed pages 1-425, ending 'END OF VOL. I.'), and vol. II opens on the continuation of that chapter and carries Books VI-VII to the work's close (vol. II printed pages 1-299, CHAP. LI). Both volumes are bound in ONE scanned item, `thomastaylor`, so the leaves are that one item's own page numbers, taken over the two runs of pages the work occupies in it -- vol. I leaves n76-n500, vol. II leaves n506-n804 -- and each run carries its own measured offset. The leaf file names keep the VOLUME prefix (v1-n76.jpg, v2-n506.jpg) because a leaf's volume is part of what a citation of it names, and because the two runs, though they do not overlap here, are the two halves of one work whose pages restart at 1 in vol. II; the ITEM is the same for both, and that is what the entries below say. The item's next work, the Elements of Theology (its own edition in this library), begins at n805, and the treatises follow it; neither is part of this work.

items.role: vol. I, the work entire (printed pp. 1-425, to Book V ch. XXXIX)
items.why: THE OFFSET IS MEASURED AT BOTH ENDS OF THE RUN, from the item's own text layer (`elementsoftheology_proclus_djvu.xml`), because this item carries NO page-number pass at all: its `_scandata.xml` has no pageNumber element and the item serves no `_page_numbers.json` (MEASURED, fetched 2026-10-05). The run is 425 leaves over the 425 numbered pages of vol. I -- one leaf per printed page, no leaf carrying two -- and the two ends fix it: n76 is printed page 1 and n500 is printed page 425, so archive n = printed page + 75. Every head that a printed page number can be read off agrees on the offset; the twenty-odd leaves whose head folio disagrees are the scan MISREADING a folio (n127's head reads '5' where 52 is due, n349's reads '2' where 274 is due), which is exactly why the offset is fixed by the ends of a run whose length equals its page count and not by a head-by-head vote.

verified.evidence: the item's own line for leaf 76 reads 'PROCLUS, THE PLATONIC SUCCESSOR, ON / The Theology of Plato. / BOOK I. CHAPTER I. / O PERICLES, to me the dearest of friends' -- the work's first page, its chapter heading and its opening words

leaf 500's first line reads 'CHAP. XXXIX. OF PLATO. 425' and its text is 'first unpolluted monad. Again, motion is the sign of vivific goodness...' -- the volume's last page, the close of ch. XXXIX. The leaf's own folio IS the number, so no arithmetic is needed here

items.role: vol. II, the Theology alone (printed pp. 1-299, Books VI-VII to the work's close CHAP. LI)
items.why: SAME ITEM AS VOL. I, its own offset: vol. II's printed pages restart at 1, and its run is 299 leaves over 299 numbered pages, so archive n = printed page + 505. The offset was already measured on this item for the Elements of Theology edition (its scan.json: n806 = printed 301, n946 = printed 441), and the two records agree -- 506 - 505 = 1 and 804 - 505 = 299 -- so the volume's offset is fixed by two independent works cut from the same scan.

verified.evidence: leaf 506 reads 'PROCLUS, THE PLATONIC SUCCESSOR, ON / The Theology of Plato. / BOOK VI. CHAPTER I. / The hebdomatic aion (eternity) therefore, of the intellectual Gods' -- vol. II's printed page 1, the continuation of the work

leaf 804's first line reads 'CHAP. LI. OF PLATO. 299' and its text is 'men only effect this partially. Plato therefore knowing that this pre-existed in the world...' -- the Theology's closing page. The next leaf, n805, is the item's NEXT work: 'THE ELEMENTS OF THEOLOGY. PROPOSITION I.' -- and the Elements edition's own import.json records its transcription as lines 40345-47601 of this same file, i.e. it begins exactly where this edition's slice ends

NOT this work: leaf 805 carries 'THE ELEMENTS OF THEOLOGY. PROPOSITION I. All multitude participates in a certain respect of the one', the first page of the volume's next work (its own edition in this library, cut from this same item at n806-n946 = printed 301-441)
